name: Spit in the Ocean Poker
description: Draw poker with one shared community card dealt face up. That card and all cards of the same rank are wild. Players get four private cards plus the community card to make a five-card hand, with a draw round and two betting rounds.

overview.description: Draw poker with one shared community card dealt face up. That card and all cards of the same rank are wild. Players get four private cards plus the community card to make a five-card hand, with a draw round and two betting rounds.

history.origins: Described in the 1926 US Playing-Card Company Official Rules as a variant of Wild Widow; one of the first shared-card poker games.
timeline: 1926: Described in US Playing-Card Company Official Rules as variant of Wild Widow.

setup.dealing: Four cards face down to each player, then one card face up to the table. The table card and all cards of the same rank are wild.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest five-card poker hand at showdown, using your four private cards plus the single community card (with wilds).
rules.gameplay: After the deal, there is a betting round. Then each player in turn may discard any number of cards and receive that many replacements from the deck. A second betting round follows, then showdown. Each hand is the player's four cards plus the community card; the table card and all cards of its rank are wild. Highest hand wins.
keyRules: Four cards per player plus one face-up community card; that card and all of same rank are wild.
One betting round after the deal, then a draw round (discard and replace), then a second betting round, then showdown.
Best five-card hand using four hole cards plus the community card wins the pot.

strategy.basic: Value the community card and its rank: if it pairs your hand or completes draws, you have hidden strength. Fold weak hands when the wild rank does not help you.
strategy.intermediate: Track how many of the wild rank are already visible; adjust your draw and betting based on whether opponents can make trips or better. Bluff when the board favors your perceived range.
strategy.advanced: Balance draw sizes to disguise hand strength; use position to check-raise or bet after the draw when the wild card creates ambiguous ranges.
tips: The single community card is wild for everyone; hands run higher than in standard draw.
Some house rules limit the draw to two cards; clarify before play.

variations.name: Max two cards draw
variations.description: Some rules allow discarding at most two cards in the draw phase instead of any number.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation only documents a common house rule; no engine overrides needed for max draw limit in this schema.

scoring.description: Highest five-card hand at showdown wins the pot. Standard poker hand rankings; the community card and all cards of its rank are wild.
scoring.winCondition: Highest five-card poker hand at showdown wins the pot.
